title: The last teaching
hookLine: Milarepa shows his student Gampopa the callouses from years of sitting: that is the secret

cards: A goodbye at a river crossing. The old man has walked his student partway down the road. Gampopa has trained with him, and now he's being sent off to practice and teach on his own.
They say their farewells, and the student bows. Then Milarepa calls him back. Wait, he says, in the story.
I have one more instruction, a very precious one. I wasn't sure I'd give it to you. Gampopa turns around, ready for the deepest secret of all.

teach.b: Milarepa turns his back to Gampopa, hitches up his robe, and shows him his backside. It's covered in thick calluses, hard as hide, from sitting on stone for years. And he says, in effect: this is it.
There's no instruction more profound than this. Practice. Sit until your seat looks like mine.
It's funny, and it's meant to be. The singer of the mountains keeps his most precious teaching for last, and it's his rear end. It's hard to retell without a grin.
Under the joke is the point. Everything Milarepa had, he got from teachings he received and then practiced, again and again, alone, in cold caves. The teaching mattered.

teach.h: A MAP LEFT IN A DRAWER.
teach.b: But a teaching that isn't practiced is a map left folded in a drawer. The calluses are what reading the map looks like after years on the road.
A student leaving a teacher wants a key, a secret, something to keep in a pocket. Milarepa gives Gampopa the opposite of a shortcut.
The secret is that there's no secret, only the long sitting.

Some hear good news in that: nothing is being held back, and there's no hidden password. There's only showing up, and showing up again. Tomorrow, the student who walked away from that river carrying it.

how: Tibetan teachers tell the story of Milarepa's last teaching to Gampopa, often with humor, to stress that steady practice matters more than any secret instruction.

practice: Feel where your body meets the seat, the weight, the pressure, the contact; that's where Milarepa's secret lives.
Stay with the breath, and when the bell rings, don't jump up: give it a few extra breaths, a little longer than you'd like.

wordCard.voice: Milarepa. The singer of the mountains, whose parting gift to his student Gampopa was his calluses from years of sitting, and no secret beyond practice. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: that's the secret. No password, no shortcut, just the seat. Day nine hundred seventy-five, done.
